name: iOS app refresh and processing tasks
plain: iOS lets apps request short refreshes (about 30 s) or longer idle processing; timing is up to the system.
meaning: The only system scheduled background work on iOS. Timing follows how often the person uses the app; dormant installs may never run.

android.note: Android periodic work min interval 15 min

ios.persistence: System decides; earliestBeginDate is a lower bound; tasks do not run after a force quit
ios.revocation: Background App Refresh off; Low Power Mode; force quit
ios.api_surface: BGAppRefreshTask (about 30 s), BGProcessingTask (minutes, idle, optional network or power), BGHealthResearchTask (iOS 17)
ios.note: App refresh about 30 s; processing minutes when idle and charging; pending request cap about 10 (unverified)

limits.headline: Can ask iPhone for short refreshes of about 30 seconds, but the system picks the time
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when iOS decides to wake the app, often after you use it a lot
can: Refresh content for about 30 seconds so it is fresh when you open the app
Run longer jobs, like cleanup or a sync, for a few minutes when the phone is idle and charging
Schedule up to about 10 pending requests
cannot: Choose the exact time; iOS can delay or skip a request
Run longer jobs while you are using the phone on battery
Repeat faster than every 15 minutes on Android, where that is the minimum
limits.reach_label: Short bursts, timed by the system
limits.differs: Android periodic work repeats at most every 15 minutes. iPhone gives no guaranteed interval.

story.what_it_is: iPhone lets apps ask for short refreshes or longer idle jobs, but the system picks the timing.

marketing.name: Background Tasks
marketing.pitch: Apple describes BGTaskScheduler as the way to refresh content and run longer jobs when the system judges it a good time.

story.for_you: You never see it. Your news or email app has fresh content when you open it because iOS ran a short refresh earlier. If you rarely open an app, it may never get a turn.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to prefetch content and sync data so the app feels instant. They cannot control the timing, so they pair it with push messages for urgent updates.

use_cases.example: A news app downloads the morning headlines in a short refresh so the front page is ready when you wake.
A podcast app fetches new episodes while your phone charges overnight in a longer processing task.
A notes app syncs your edits to the cloud in the background so another device is up to date.
A store app refreshes your order status so the screen is already current when you open it.
A health app processes a day of sensor data while you sleep and charge your phone.
An ad and measurement tool uses the short window to upload queued events from the day.

risks: Can be used to poll for signals
story.android_note: Android periodic work has a 15 minute minimum interval.
story.ios_note: App refresh is about 30 seconds. Idle processing runs for minutes when charging.
